title: irigtime report v1 revision 8 — stable
$comment: Version-pinned release artifact identifier (resolves when v0.8.0 is published). Schema frozen after the reviewed draft; no tag or publication is performed by this PR.
description: Producer validation is strict (unknown producer keys fail). Consumers MUST ignore unknown fields within a supported schema_version, accept additive schema_revision increases, and reject unsupported schema_version values. Every defined key is always emitted; null meaning is per field. Incompatible changes require a new schema_version and breaking tool release. All usize and signed/unsigned 64/128-bit values are decimal strings, including future fields; small wire/date fields remain integers. Suffix units: _ns nanoseconds, _ms milliseconds, _bytes bytes, _rtc 100 ns RTC ticks, _unix_s Unix-style UTC seconds since1970; clock_count_ns is native year-relative time, not Unix. Output is ASCII-only JSON (non-ASCII uses Unicode escapes); ordering is deterministic. Draft->stable is an explicit reviewed revision change. This is CLI output only, not an IRIG 106 wire standard or a JSON loading API. Complete reports are produced on exits 0/1; no report is started on usage/input exits 2/3. On output failure 4 a partial or even complete byte stream may already have been written: consumers must discard it. Existing stderr diagnostics are retained; findings are per command. A revision MAY add values to options.command, row kind and similar enums for newly supported views. Consumers MUST treat unknown enum values as an unsupported view, not an error. Reserved shapes such as rows MAY gain fields until first emitted.

schema_version.description: Major schema contract; incompatible shape/type/unit/meaning changes require a new version and a breaking tool release.

schema_revision.description: Additive revision8 records explicit options.ntp_era and caller-declared-era clock basis/coverage values; no automatic era guessing.

schema_status.description: Stable contract following the reviewed draft-to-stable transition at revision 2. Further contract changes follow the version and revision rules.

tool.description: Producer identity and optional build provenance.

library_version.description: Exactly lockstep library version used by the CLI.

source_revision.description: Build-supplied IRIGTIME_SOURCE_REVISION, else GitHub Actions GITHUB_SHA, else null. Release builds must set IRIGTIME_SOURCE_REVISION to the actual release commit; PR GITHUB_SHA may identify a temporary merge commit. Never probes Git at runtime.

input.description: Input provenance; never canonicalizes or makes the user path absolute.

name.description: File name exactly as supplied, decoded lossily if needed; never made absolute.

name_lossy.description: True iff name required replacement characters; native_name_hex preserves its exact representation.

native_name_hex.description: Lowercase hexadecimal POSIX filename bytes or Windows UTF-16LE code units; includes unpaired surrogates.

size_bytes.description: Input size in bytes from the opened file metadata. A digest may be added in a later revision.

options.description: Effective options used for this command.

fail_on.description: Effective finding exit threshold; `never` disables exit 1 only, not operational exits 2/3/4.

threshold_ms.description: Effective scanner jump threshold in milliseconds: summary uses 1000, jumps uses the selected value; null for channels (not evaluated). Also null for timeline (jumps not evaluated). Also null for correlate.

limit.description: Effective maximum emitted packet rows for timeline, as decimal count; null for commands where not applicable. Entire input is still analysed.

query_rtc.description: Requested header RTC counter query in100ns ticks, decimal string; null outside correlate. Counter selection is not a data/time-channel association.

ntp_era.description: Explicit caller NTP era for the whole input, decimal string -14..=59 (eras overlapping Gregorian years0..=9999); null means no era declaration and no conversion/guess for nonzero NTP. PTP/F1 unaffected.

highest_level.description: Highest observed command-specific level, regardless of fail_on; null if no findings. Drives exit 1 only at/above fail_on.

findings.description: Command-specific findings; stderr diagnostics retain the existing command behaviour.

report.description: One shared text/JSON report projection. Qualification remains observed inventory until governing joining is implemented.

rows.description: Packet rows for timeline (at most options.limit); null for inventory and correlate. CSV is its own separate machine format, not a JSON envelope view.

total_packets.description: Number of complete framed packets in the file.

time_packets.description: Number of time packets, BOTH 0x11 (Format 1) and 0x12 (Format 2).

references_seen.description: Total admitted absolute references observed, including evicted references.

reference_count.description: Current bounded compatibility-correlator reference cache size.

references_evicted.description: References removed from that cache by eviction or reset; not lost report segments.

first_rtc.description: Header RTC of the first complete packet in FILE ORDER, on any channel across resets; 100 ns ticks; null if not observed.

last_rtc.description: Header RTC of the last complete packet in FILE ORDER, on any channel across resets; 100 ns ticks; null if not observed.

rtc_duration_ns.description: Forward modular first-to-last RTC elapsed ns only with no detected resets; null if unavailable due to resets or no endpoints (as in text).

channels.description: Channel inventory sorted by ascending channel ID.

data_types.description: Observed packet types sorted by numeric ID.

packets.description: Complete packet count for this type.

jumps.description: null means NOT EVALUATED (channels); evaluated count 0 means no jump detected (summary/jumps).

correlation.description: Counter-query report for correlate; null for other commands. Packet rows remain null because a requested counter has no packet identity.

policy.description: Effective CLI compatibility policy for this entire report, present even without findings. This is not a library SharedPolicy snapshot or a data-source association.

unsigned.description: Nonnegative decimal string; all usize/u64/u128 quantities use this representation.

signed.description: Signed decimal string; all i64/i128 quantities use this representation.

maybe_unsigned.description: Decimal string or null; null meaning is defined at each field.

level.description: Shared --fail-on finding severity, from most to least severe.

scale.description: Time scale; unknown means no scale qualification is available.

basis.description: Origin of a scale qualification, never Rust Debug text.

clock.description: Observed civil clock; no Unix epoch is implied. Native leap label 60 is retained.

year.description: Calendar year (native domain 0..9999), or null when unknown; never inferred from the host clock.

second.description: Second of minute, including an explicit leap label 60.

clock_count_ns.description: Nanoseconds since day 1 00:00:00 within the represented year; not Unix time.

scale.description: Scale of this clock, after any labelled conversion.

basis.description: How this clock scale was established; derived, leap table denotes PTP TAI->UTC.

year_offset.description: Count of report-detected forward year rollovers within this reset segment; not an absolute year.

segment.description: One admitted-reference reset segment on one channel; never combines different reset segments.

index.description: One-based per-channel reset segment index, in observation order.

first.description: First admitted clock in file observation order in this segment; null if not observed.

last.description: Last admitted clock in file observation order in this segment; null if not observed.

first_rtc.description: Header RTC of the first admitted reference in this segment; 100 ns ticks; null if not observed.

last_rtc.description: Header RTC of the last admitted reference in this segment; 100 ns ticks; null if not observed.

channel.description: File-wide observed time-channel inventory. Last format/status attributes describe the latest decoded CSDW; first/last can span resets. Consult segments for isolated clocks.

id.description: Channel ID from the packet header; rows sort ascending.

packets.description: Observed Format 1/2 packet count represented by this channel inventory.

format.description: Closed native format name. reserved carries its wire value in format_reserved; unknown means not observed.

format_reserved.description: Raw reserved FMT or NTF nibble; null unless format is reserved.

native_scale.description: Native payload scale before conversion; does not qualify the converted first/last clocks.

scale_basis.description: Basis for native_scale, using the same vocabulary as clock.basis.

date_format.description: Latest Format 1 DATE field; null when not applicable (Format 2) or not observed.

leap_year.description: Latest Format 1 LY flag; null when not applicable (Format 2) or not observed.

format2_word.description: Raw Format 2 CSDW u32; null when not applicable or not observed.

status.description: Explicit Format 2 TS spelling; reserved retains status_raw; null when not applicable/not observed.

status_raw.description: Raw Format 2 TS nibble; null when not applicable/not observed.

format1_low_nibble.description: Raw low nibble, not an unqualified SRC assertion: edition/EXT qualification remains necessary. Null for Format 2 or unobserved.

segment_count.description: Number of admitted-reference segments on this channel; starts at 1 when a reference is admitted, otherwise 0.

segments.description: All admitted-reference segments, in per-channel index order; disk-spooled, not retained in RAM.

first.description: First admitted clock in file order across all segments; null if not observed. May have a different scale/basis from last.

last.description: Last admitted clock in file order across all segments; null if not observed.

first_rtc.description: Header RTC of the first admitted reference in file order across resets; 100 ns ticks; null if not observed.

last_rtc.description: Header RTC of the last admitted reference in file order across resets; 100 ns ticks; null if not observed.

min_gap_ns.description: Minimum non-backward same-segment reference-pair spacing in ns; null if no eligible pair was evaluated.

max_gap_ns.description: Maximum non-backward same-segment reference-pair spacing in ns; null if no eligible pair was evaluated.

jump.description: Sampled native clock discontinuity in observation order, bounded to the first 20.

index.description: Zero-based global admitted-reference observation index, not per-channel and not packet index.

expected_ns.description: Expected native day-1 clock count in ns, including unwrapped year span when applicable; not Unix time.

actual_ns.description: Actual native day-1 clock count in ns, including unwrapped year span when applicable; not Unix time.

expected_year_days.description: 365/366 day basis for expected_ns; null when unknown.

actual_year_days.description: 365/366 unwrapped year basis for actual_ns; null when no year unwrap was applied.

finding.description: One sampled command-specific finding; all location keys are present.

level.description: Owner-approved TF severity or documented CLI scanner severity.

code.description: TF-nnn when explicitly identified; null for CLI diagnostics without an assigned TF code.

message.description: Human diagnostic without a Rust Debug severity prefix; wording is not a machine identifier.

channel.description: Packet channel ID when known; null for file-wide or unlocated diagnostics.

packet.description: Zero-based file packet observation index when known; null for file-wide/unlocated diagnostics.

findings.description: Per-command exact counts and bounded samples; commands can evaluate different facts (channels does not evaluate jumps).

omitted.description: Total finding count minus number of emitted samples.

samples.description: First findings in observation order; at most 20.

jumps.description: Jump evaluation over admitted non-backward pairs.

omitted.description: Exact jump count minus number of emitted samples.

samples.description: First jump samples in observation order; at most 20.

row.description: One shared packet observation: numeric absolute clock or explicit counter-only result. Correlate ambiguity candidates remain reserved. No data/time-channel association is inferred.

kind.description: Counter-only and ambiguity are explicit, never silently converted to a chosen absolute answer.

candidates.description: Reserved labelled source/segment candidates. Timeline emits an empty array: the direct clock does not establish a data/time-channel or segment association.

issue.description: Context issue; null if there is none.

offset_bytes.description: Byte offset of the packet header in the input file, decimal string.

data_type.description: Packet data-type code from the header.

association.description: Qualification seam states. Conflicting and unestablished are unresolved for source/segment answers; timeline currently emits unestablished only. Numeric channel equality is not evidence.

clock.description: Native calendar resolution or null when counter-only. Selected references retain F1 stated FMT / assumed UTC RDG-009 or PTP covered/stale table basis; RTC or unavailable lineage remains unknown/unresolved. This does not establish data-channel association.

network_time.description: The packet CSDW, independently of its resolved clock or admission. Null means no applicable Format2 facts (non-F2/missing CSDW or no selected F2 answer respectively); raw reserved values remain facts, never imply GPS.

clock.description: Candidate clock or null when unresolved.

query_value.description: Any-channel native result; no silent selection across resets.

clock.description: Numeric native query clock, or null when unresolved. The selected reference retains its F1 stated/assumed or PTP table basis; RTC or unavailable lineage remains unknown/unresolved.

issue.description: Native unresolved context/error; null when clock is present. Any-channel may be withheld across resets or absent references.

network_time.description: The reference selected by the numeric correlator, not the channel latest observation. Null means no applicable Format2 facts (non-F2/missing CSDW or no selected F2 answer respectively); raw reserved values remain facts, never imply GPS.

query_answer.description: One native printed channel answer. Ordinary answers sort by channel; reset answers follow segment closure then final channel order. This is counter-query policy, not data-channel association.

channel.description: Queried time-channel ID, not an associated data-channel ID.

segment.description: One-based per-channel reset segment, decimal string. Unreset channels have segment1.

labelled.description: True when text explicitly labels the reset segment.

clock.description: Numeric native query clock, or null when unresolved. Scale/basis follow the selected reference: IRIG assumes UTC RDG-009, FMT4 states UTC, FMT5 states GPS, PTP uses its conversion table; RTC/unavailable lineage stays unknown. No year or data-channel association is inferred.

issue.description: Native unresolved context/error; null when clock is present. Any-channel may be withheld across resets or absent references.

network_time.description: The reference selected by the numeric correlator, not the channel latest observation. Null means no applicable Format2 facts (non-F2/missing CSDW or no selected F2 answer respectively); raw reserved values remain facts, never imply GPS.

query_report.description: Same native report as correlate text; every matching reset segment is retained, without choosing a silent winner.

any.description: Any-channel result, or explicit reason for withholding it across resets/no references.

answers.description: Printed per-channel/segment native answers, streamed one at a time. Can contain unresolved segment clocks; per-channel failures omitted by text remain in command findings.

network_time.description: 106-24R1 Figure11-15 NTF and TS wire fields; observation is distinct from successful conversion.

protocol.description: Protocol/revision selected by NTF; reserved retains its raw ntf.

status.description: TS0 not-valid,TS1 valid,TS2..15 reserved; not an invented absolute answer.

report_policy.description: Versioned effective CLI settings; current legacy correlation is reported honestly, not relabelled as a native recording policy.

id.description: Versioned CLI correlation algorithm identity; deliberately distinct from library SharedPolicy IDs. Change on algorithm change.

defaults_id.description: Versioned CLI defaults catalog; change when fixed defaults change. Effective command overrides remain in options.

ntp_era_source.description: Explicit era context for this input: caller-declared iff options.ntp_era is non-null, otherwise none. All-zero raw NTP remains the unsynchronized sentinel.

ntp_era_inference.description: No pivot, era0 guess, host clock or dated F1 inference is used by this CLI.

reference_selection.description: Actual legacy nearest-reference numeric counter-offset algorithm, not Standard/Interpolate mode.

drift_correction.description: Whether the CLI numeric correlator applies drift correction; currently false.

reference_window_ns.description: Actual live-cache age window in ns; main global age and isolated per-channel ages share the default. Counter queries use separate target brackets.

reference_cap.description: Reference-count cap per main live cache and per combined isolated pool; not a total-report memory count and not a target-query cap.

query_reference_storage.description: Target-specific bracketing independent of live-cache eviction; preserves old requested RTCs.

query_candidates_per_channel.description: Maximum retained candidates per queried channel, including duplicate representatives, across two RTC groups.

reset_backward_step_ns.description: Immediate reset for a backward step strictly greater than this bound, ns; a reader heuristic, not a wire reset flag.

reset_backward_comparison.description: Strict threshold: equality alone is out-of-order, not immediate reset.

reset_run_references.description: Consecutive behind-baseline references needed to declare the short-reset run at its first packet.

reset_run_order.description: The reset run must increase strictly among its members while all remain behind the accepted baseline.

leap_table.description: Table actually installed in the scanner, even if no PTP value uses it; identity/currency do not imply every reported clock is covered.

finding_sample_cap.description: Maximum retained first finding messages; exact per-level counts include all omitted findings.

jump_sample_cap.description: Maximum retained jump samples; jumps.count and omitted remain exact independently.

policy_leap_table.description: Installed table provenance and declared UTC currency. No host clock is consulted.

id.description: Actual installed leap table identity, including the built-in source-content hash.

source.description: Authority/source description supplied with the table; runtime does not fetch it.

supported_start_unix_s.description: First supported UTC second, inclusive, Unix seconds; no offset is guessed before support.

known_current_through_unix_s.description: Final covered UTC second, inclusive of all its fractions, Unix seconds. Later PTP UTC uses the last known offset and TF-021.

entries.description: Actual installed transition-entry count; does not equal the coverage end.
